page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of evaluated instances. Multi-core CPU performance and general computational workloads, such as Geekbench software compilation and ray tracing, fall within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 565.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weaker, registering at 37.36 GB/sec and 14.86 GB/sec respectively.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the c3d-standard-8 is suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, Redis database operations, and basic text or image processing. It can handle lightweight machine learning tasks, such as prompt processing for small 135M parameter models, but exhibits poor performance on larger models like the 7B parameter variant. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a standard hardware profile with dedicated resources, making it a predictable option for mid-tier application hosting and development environments where local NVMe storage is not required.
